t: That payment and settlement of mileage and other travel allowance accounts of all military personnel, when such accounts are authorized to be based on distances between given points, shall be made in accordance with distances established for payment and settlement of mileage accounts of officers pursuant to the provisions of the Act of June 12, 1906, as amended (34 Stat. 246; 10 U. S. C. 870).

fable.w: This provision only standardizes how mileage and travel allowance accounts of military personnel are calculated, by reference to distances already established under a prior Act. There is no tempting participation reading: no outside party is consulted, no hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue is involved. It is purely an internal federal payment rule.
fable.s: shall be made in accordance with distances established for payment and settlement of mileage accounts of officers

qwen_block.w: This section establishes the administrative procedure for calculating travel allowances for military personnel based on statutory distances. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making input from parties outside the federal government. The actors involved are military personnel and federal officials administering the payment.
qwen_block.s: That payment and settlement of mileage and other travel allowance accounts of all military personnel, when such accounts are authorized to be based on distances between given points, shall be made in accordance with distances established for payment and settlement of mileage accounts of officers pursuant to the provisions of the Act of June 12, 1906, as amended (34 Stat. 246; 10 U. S. C. 870).

opus.w: This section only says how military mileage and travel allowance accounts are paid and settled, using distances already set under the 1906 Act. It does not involve any outside party, such as a state, expert, company or member of the public, in a federal decision. Words like "settlement" and "established" describe internal payment administration, not an outside group taking part in a decision, so nothing here meets the definition.
opus.b:
1. **Step 1:** You might be tempted to read "settlement of... accounts" or "established... pursuant to the provisions of the Act" as a federal decision-making process. That reading fails. The section only says which distance tables to use when paying military travel allowances. No one outside the federal government is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue.
